target.title: fix(cli): show exit code when plugin npm install returns empty output
target.body:
Closes #98484

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `openclaw plugins install @openclaw/acpx` (or the ACPX plugin step of `openclaw update`) would see a completely blank failure message when npm exited non-zero without writing anything to stdout or stderr. The visible output was:

```
Downloading @openclaw/acpx...
Extracting /tmp/openclaw-hook-pack-...
npm install failed:
Also not a valid hook pack: Error: package.json missing openclaw.hooks
```

The first line ends after the colon with nothing after it, so users cannot tell whether npm was killed, timed out, hit a proxy failure, or crashed. The trailing hook-pack fallback message is a red herring for a plugin-only package like `@openclaw/acpx`, but with no primary detail to read, that misleading line is all users have to work with.

## Why This Change Was Made

`installPackageDir` was building the failure string as `` `npm install failed: ${npmRes.stderr.trim() || npmRes.stdout.trim()}` ``. When both streams were empty, that produced `npm install failed: ` with no trailing detail. The `SpawnResult` returned by `runCommandWithTimeout` already carries the useful signal (`code`, `signal`, and `termination`), but it was being discarded.

Extract a small `formatNpmDependencyInstallFailure` helper that keeps npm's own output when it exists (the primary source of truth) but falls back to the exit code, signal, and termination reason when both streams are empty. This is a strictly additive change to the failure branch: successful installs, non-empty-stderr installs, and the existing exception path are untouched.

## User Impact

Users hitting this failure now see something they can act on instead of an empty line, for example:

- `npm install failed: exit code 1 (no output from npm)`
- `npm install failed: timed out, signal SIGTERM (no output from npm)`
- `npm install failed: signal SIGKILL (no output from npm)`

The trailing hook-pack fallback line is unchanged (that is a separate concern outside this fix), but users can now see the real underlying npm exit signal and stop chasing the misleading "missing openclaw.hooks" message. When npm does produce output, behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

Ran the affected file both ways.

Before the fix (regression tests fail with the exact user-reported symptom):

```
❯ src/infra/install-package-dir.test.ts (15 tests | 2 failed)
   ✓ surfaces npm stderr when dependency install fails
   × includes exit code when npm dependency install fails with empty stdout and stderr
      AssertionError: expected 'npm install failed: ' to contain 'exit code 1'
      Expected: "exit code 1"
      Received: "npm install failed: "
   × includes signal detail when npm dependency install is killed by a signal
      AssertionError: expected 'npm install failed: ' to contain 'SIGKILL'
```

After the fix (all 15 pass, including the existing stderr-surfacing test that guards the "keep npm's own output when it exists" path):

```
✓ src/infra/install-package-dir.test.ts (15 tests) 733ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  15 passed (15)
```

Lint clean on both changed files:

```
❯ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/infra/install-package-dir.ts src/infra/install-package-dir.test.ts
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
Finished in 6.9s on 2 files with 242 rules using 1 threads.
```

Scope stayed inside `src/infra/install-package-dir.*`:

```
❯ git diff main..HEAD --stat
 src/infra/install-package-dir.test.ts | 94 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 src/infra/install-package-dir.ts      | 38 +++++++++++++-
 2 files changed, 131 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)
```

The wider `pnpm test` infra shard had one pre-existing failure in `src/infra/exec-approvals-analysis.test.ts` unrelated to this change (a regex asserts `python3(?:\.\d+)?` at the end of the resolved command path, but on this host the Homebrew Python lives at `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/python@3.14/...`, which puts `python@3.14` earlier in the path). Verified the same failure reproduces on `main` before applying the fix.

## AI disclosure

This change was written with the assistance of Claude. I have reviewed the diff and the tests and take responsibility for the code.
